Over 6,000 cases pending with Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunals in Rangpur
item.description:
More than 6,000 cases remain pending with three Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunals in Rangpur, with over 300 rape and dowry cases awaiting trial for five to 18 years, leaving victims and accused trapped in prolonged legal battles.
Over 2,000 of the pending cases involve rape, while victims say repeated court appearances and mounting legal expenses have pushed many families into financial hardship.
A visit to the tribunals revealed the plight of litigants who have spent years seeking justice. Sharifa Yasmin, from Anandanagar village in Pirgachha upazila, said her husband and in-laws drove her out of their home because she could not pay Tk200,000 in dowry.
She filed a case six years ago, but the trial has yet to begin. With hearings scheduled roughly every two months, Sharifa said she had sold cattle, goats, ducks and chickens to cover travel costs and court-related expenses.
Other women, including Asma Begum of Pirgachha and Mariam Begum of Rangpur Sadar, also described similar experiences.
Asma, a poor woman, said her daughter was abducted and raped eight years ago, but the trial had yet to begin.
Sohrab Hossain of Bhandarbari village in Pirgachha said he had been attending court for 18 years in connection with a rape case filed against him. Working as a rickshaw puller in Dhaka, he returns to Rangpur every two months for hearings.
He said he could not afford to miss a hearing for fear of an arrest warrant, forcing him to spend money on repeated journeys while struggling to earn a living.
Human rights activists and legal experts blamed the delays on a shortage of judges, police failures to produce witnesses and a lack of diligence by those involved in prosecution.
Rumana Zaman, president of Rangpur district chapter of Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, said the law sets time limits for disposing of cases involving violence against women and children, yet many litigants spend years waiting for justice. She called for more judges to expedite trials.
Rights activist Monowara Begum warned that the failure to punish offenders was allowing violence, rape and dowry-related abuse to persist. She also urged authorities to increase the number of judges and ensure speedy trials.
Shafi Kamal, special public prosecutor at Tribunal-1, said nearly 2,000 cases were awaiting trial at his court. He cited the absence of complainants and witnesses on scheduled dates, along with other procedural complications, as reasons for the growing backlog. He said judges and prosecutors were working to ensure justice for litigants.
Moksedul Haque, special public prosecutor at Tribunal-2, said they were also trying to expedite proceedings.
Legal experts called for a dedicated cell to speed up the disposal of cases involving violence against women and children in Rangpur, alongside stricter monitoring by the High Court.

item.title: Health Minister: Community clinics to be renamed family welfare centres
item.description:
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Saturday announced that all community clinics across the country will be renamed family welfare centres as part of plans to expand healthcare services at union level.
He made the announcement while outlining the government’s plans to improve healthcare infrastructure and services during surprise visits to several health facilities in Mymensingh.
Earlier in the day, the minister visited Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes before inspecting Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, where he expressed dissatisfaction over various irregularities, including medical equipment found in a garbage dump and doctors and nurses failing to report to work on time.
During his visit to the hospital around noon, he inspected the labour ward, measles isolation ward and dengue ward. He also examined the quality of treatment, the ward environment and the condition of washrooms.
The minister expressed anger after finding rubbish on the ground floor of the hospital's new building. He also ordered a swift investigation and the submission of a report into the discovery of used cannulas, syringes and other medical equipment in the hospital's garbage dump.
He said action would be taken against those found negligent in their duties, including staff who failed to arrive at the hospital on time. The minister also questioned why a patient in the gynaecology ward had to purchase saline from outside and instructed the hospital authorities to take necessary measures.
He further sought an explanation for the delay in submitting an investigation report into a fire at the hospital more than a month ago. The authorities told him that the report has been delayed due to holidays.
Earlier, during his visits to Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes, he said the government planned to upgrade both health complexes to 151-bed facilities.
A large-scale tendering process worth around Tk 16,000 crore for the health sector would be launched within the next 15 to 20 days, he said, adding that steps would be taken to ensure the supply of necessary medicines to the community clinics after they are renamed family welfare centres.

item.title: Dengue: 6 more die, 1,898 hospitalized in 24 hrs
item.description:
Six more people died of dengue and 1,898 new patients were hospitalized across the country in 24 hours until 8:00am on Saturday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 376 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, two were reported in Chittagong division and one each in Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna and Rajshahi divisions, it said.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 121,699 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 115,132 have recovered.

item.title: Health minister orders nurse transfer, salary cuts for four doctors
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Saturday paid a surprise visit to Phulpur Upazila Health Complex in the district and ordered transfer of a nurse for negligence of duty.
He also directed deduction of one day’s salary of four doctors for remaining absent from their workplace without prior permission, said a press release.
After the inspection, the health minister told journalists that the government is working to bring the country’s health sector to a level that meets public expectations and ensures people’s satisfaction, in line with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s directives.
Noting that the government has taken various initiatives to resolve long-standing problems in the health sector, he said, “Cleanliness activities at hospitals are being strengthened, medicine supplies are being increased and adequate stocks of saline have been ensured.”
Sakhawat expressed the hope that significant progress in the health sector would become visible within the next few months.
He also said the government plans to invite tenders worth several thousand crore taka within the next 15 days as part of its efforts to develop and restructure the health sector.
This tender is aimed at improving various healthcare institutions across the country, including upazila health complexes, the minister said.
Besides, he said, initiatives are being taken to establish modern pathological laboratories at upazila-level hospitals so that diagnostic facilities can be expanded at the grassroots level.
Later, the minister made another surprise visit to the nearby Tarakanda Upazila Health Complex in Mymensingh.

item.title: Two killed, 15 injured in bus-truck collision in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
Two passengers were killed and 15 others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger bus and a truck in the Bertala area of Sarail upazila in Brahmanbaria on Saturday morning.
The accident occurred at around 8:30am on the Dhaka-Sylhet Highway. The deceased were identified as Sourav and Asif, both from Parbatipur in Dinajpur. However, Asif’s full identity could not be confirmed. Of the injured, 3 were sent to Dhaka in critical condition.
Police and local residents said a passenger bus operated by Diganta Paribahan, traveling from Rangpur to Sylhet, collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction in the Berotola area of Sarail upazila.
Several passengers sustained serious injuries in the collision. They were rescued and taken to hospital, while 3 critically injured passengers were sent to Dhaka for advanced treatment.

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Textiles and Jute on Saturday recommended mechanizing operations under the Bangladesh Sericulture Development Board and ensuring easier access to yarn, dyes and raw materials for marginal weavers.
The committee made the recommendations at its first meeting of the 13th National Parliament at the National Parliamnet with its Chairman Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia, MP, in the chair.
The committee also recommended ensuring transparency, integrity and accountability in the tender process by avoiding repeated awards of tenders to the same institution and providing opportunities to other eligible institutions.
It suggested involving local members of parliament in taking necessary steps to make yarn, dyes and other raw materials more accessible to marginal weavers through weavers' associations or the appointment of dealers, said a press release of parliament secretariat.
The committee further recommended examining the operations of the Bangladesh Handloom Board's office at Ranir Bandar in Dinajpur and verifying whether the land associated with the office had been leased out or allocated through other means before taking necessary action.
At the meeting, the committee reviewed the activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute and its subordinate departments and agencies. Officials presented an overview of their operations and briefed the committee on the ministry's initiatives under the government's 180-day program and the progress of ongoing projects.
The committee also recommended conducting all activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute in line with the prime minister's election manifesto and taking appropriate and necessary initiatives to implement its commitments.
At the beginning of the meeting, the chairman paid tribute to Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, former BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the Great War of Liberation. He prayed for the salvation of their souls.

Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, MP, State Minister Md Shariful Alam, MP, and committee members S M Faisal, MP, Md Abdullah MP, Rezeka Sultana, MP, Md Afjal Hossain MP, Hafez Muhammad Rabiul Bashar, MP, and Mahabuba Hakim, MP, attended the meeting.

item.title: Madhumati embankment breach sparks erosion fears
item.description:
A 52-metre section of a protective embankment along the Madhumati River has developed a breach near Fukra Launch Ghat in Gopalganj’s Kashiani upazila, raising fears of further erosion and threatening nearby homes, farmland, roads and institutions.
Built about 10 years ago, the 2.5km embankment had helped bring river erosion under control. However, a breach that appeared on September 23 has renewed concerns among residents, who are demanding permanent protection.
Several other sections of the embankment are also at risk, as the soil beneath the structure is suspected to have been washed away.
The Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) began placing sandbags at the site on October 10. Around 5,000 sandbags have been placed to contain the erosion, said Md Koushik Gazi, a work assistant at the BWDB’s Bhatia Para sub-divisional engineer’s office in Kashiani.
He said the river’s narrow, deep channel and a bend near Fukra Launch Ghat had contributed to the problem. As water levels began to recede about a month ago, the current intensified, triggering the breach.
The full extent of the damage would become clear once water levels fell further, allowing officials to assess the condition of the embankment, Gazi added.
BWDB Gopalganj Executive Engineer Md Shawkat Osman said temporary measures were underway to prevent further erosion, while a feasibility study for permanent protection was in progress.
“Once the study is completed, we plan to construct a permanent protective embankment near Fukra Launch Ghat under a project,” he said.
Local residents Md Mintu Munshi and Alamgir Hossain Zakir said erosion had already destroyed homes, farmland and trees in the area. They said nearly two kilometres of land on the Gopalganj side had been eroded, while chars had emerged across the river in Lohagara upazila of Narail.
The renewed erosion has put remaining homes, cropland, roads and educational and religious institutions at risk, they said, urging the authorities to build a permanent embankment.
Abir Alamgir Piyas, a first-year honours student at Ramdia SK Government College, said generations of local residents had lost their ancestral land to river erosion.
“The erosion has started again, putting whatever property we have left at risk. My family and many others are living in fear,” he said, calling for permanent protection.

item.title: Banned Chhatra League, Jubo League activists attack police in Gopalganj, injure 2
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League and Jubo League attacked police in Gopalganj on Saturday afternoon, vandalizing a police vehicle and beating 2 police personnel, according to police.
The incident took place around noon in the Raghunathpur ferry terminal area of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. Activists of the 2 organizations were seen taking part in the attack with sticks.
A video of the incident has circulated on social media, with several Chhatra League activists who took part in the procession sharing it on their Facebook accounts.
The video shows processionists carrying sticks from Charpara road in Raghunathpur and arriving at the ferry terminal area. They chanted “Joy Bangla” before attacking and vandalizing a police vehicle on patrol. Police personnel left the scene in the vehicle immediately after the vandalism.
Gopalganj Sadar police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Aminul Islam said: “Police were conducting routine patrols in the Bedgram ferry terminal area under Sadar police station. At that time, several people were marching in support of Sheikh Hasina, led by banned Jubo League leader Milan and Chhatra League leader Mursalin. When police tried to stop them, the processionists attacked the police with sticks. 2 police personnel, including Sadar police station Sub-Inspector Phul Mia, were injured. The police vehicle was also vandalized. The officers then left the scene in the vehicle.”
The OC further said: “The 2 injured police personnel received primary treatment at Gopalganj 250-bed General Hospital. An operation is underway to arrest members of the banned Jubo League and Chhatra League involved in the attack and vehicle vandalism. Additional police have been deployed in the area.”
Senior police officials visited the scene after receiving news of the attack. The area remained tense following the incident.
Police and other law enforcement personnel have strengthened security measures and set up checkpoints at key locations across the district to maintain normalcy following the attack and vandalism.

item.description:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by an emergency medical team on Friday after collapsing during training, the club said.
"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session with FC Bayern's reserve team," Bayern said on their website.
"Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations at the hospital and will remain under medical care."
Kompany, the 40-year-old former Manchester City defender, missed training and a press conference on Tuesday ahead of Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.
"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body -- and then at some point my body just said, 'enough is enough!'" Kompany said after the Arsenal game.
On Friday, Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl said the health of their coach "is our top priority".
"We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he recovers quickly. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties."
English assistant coach Aaron Danks took training and handled the press conference ahead of the Arsenal game.
"It affected his legs at times; he was experiencing some pain. It's just a virus. He needs rest," Danks said on Tuesday.
"The most important thing we're encouraging him to do right now is to rest and take as much time as he needs—no matter how long that may be."
Bundesliga leaders Bayern visit Freiburg, who are third in the table, on Saturday.
Their next Champions League match is on November 3 in Madrid against Atletico.
The Spanish club posted their best wishes on social media.
"We wish you a speedy recovery. We hope to see you here in Madrid, on the bench, in a few days," wrote the Spanish club adding a heart emoji.
Kompany, a centre back, started his career with Anderlecht in his native Brussels. He moved to Hamburg and then to Manchester City as one of the club's last signings before the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008.
He went on to play 360 games for the club, where he was also captain for eight season as the team became the dominant force in English football.
He played 89 times for Belgium and finished his playing career back at Anderlecht in 2019 where he was player-coach in the first of his three seasons in charge
He took over at Burnley in 2022, leading them to a Championship title in 2023 but the club was relegated the next season with their lowest ever points total.
Bayern, who had just endured a trophyless season and had been unable to persuade Thomas Tuchel to stay, sprung a surprise by paying Burnley to sign Kompany as manager in 2024.
He led the club two the Bundesliga title each of his first two seasons and to a German Cup in 2026. After six games, Bayern lead the table this season on goal difference. In 74 Bundesliga games under Kompany, Bayern have won 57 and lost three.
Kompany completed an MBA at Manchester Business School in 2018.

item.title: Summer Athletics 2026: Imranur, Shirin claim 100m gold
item.description:
Bangladesh Navy’s sprinters Imranur Rahman and Shirin Akter dominated the men’s and women’s 100 metres respectively in the 18th Koko National Summer Athletics competition, as fresh promises were made to improve athletes’ accommodation, nutrition and transport facilities.
On the first day of the competition held at National Stadium on Friday, Imranur clocked 10.53 seconds to win the men’s 100m gold, finishing ahead of his fellow Navy sprinter Mohammad Ismail, who took silver in 10.67 seconds. Army’s Tarek Rahman claimed bronze in 10.73 seconds.
Shirin won the women’s 100m title in 12.08 seconds. Army’s Sharifa Khatun finished second in 12.23 seconds, while Navy’s Sumaiya Dewan took third place in 12.33 seconds.
Shirin credited her success to the support of her teammates, coach and sporting organisations.
“Alhamdulillah, by the infinite mercy of Allah, it feels wonderful to finish first,” she said after winning the coveted gold.
She acknowledged the contributions of coach Abdullah Hel Kafi, Bangladesh Navy, Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishtan (BKSP), Bangladesh Athletics Federation and Bangladesh Olympic Association to her achievement.
Shirin also expressed hope that the performance would boost her preparations for the upcoming South Asian competitions.
Meanwhile, Imranur stressed the need to improve facilities for athletes, saying initiatives were being taken to address their accommodation, food, nutritional and transport needs.
Efforts are also being made to encourage more athletes from district-level competitions to participate, with greater coordination among the relevant organisations.
Organisers expect improved accommodation, nutritious meals and transport support to encourage wider participation and help identify emerging talent across the country.
Earlier, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir formally inaugurated the meet as the chief guest.
State Minister for Youth and Sports Md. Aminul Haque addressed the event as a special guest while Bangladesh Athletics Federation (BAF) general secretary Advocate Ali Imam Tapan delivered the welcome address with BAF President Mohammad Abdullah Zaber in the chair.

item.description:
Water Resources Minister and BNP Joint Secretary General Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee on Friday called for a united social movement to protect people's dignity and build a better society, saying the people had suffered significant losses over the past 17 years and did not want to lose anything more.
He made the call while addressing a meeting organised by Life Line Welfare Organization at Ayesha High School field in Totakhil under Chandraganj upazila of Lakshmipur.
Anee urged people to remain united against social problems and work collectively to build a better society, noting that the country had been regained through struggle and sacrifice.
"Do not issue threats of a one-point movement; there is no benefit in making such threats," he said, adding that the BNP had emerged from the streets through movements and struggles and would not be intimidated.
He alleged that Jamaat-e-Islami had colluded with the Awami League and enforced strikes and blockades for 172 days in 1996.
The minister also described Islami Chhatra Shibir as a clandestine organisation that had operated at various universities before August 5, urging people to remain vigilant.
Criticising opposition parties, Anee alleged that they were obstructing the government outside Parliament despite delivering eloquent speeches inside the House.
Political parties, he said, should focus on national and social development rather than confining their activities to rallies and meetings.
Anee also called for collective efforts to counter religious misinterpretations, misinformation and drug abuse, warning that those involved in such activities would not be spared regardless of their influence.

Senior Station Officer of Faridpur Fire Service Sribas Baroi said the truck reportedly lost control and overturned, causing the accident. The injured were receiving treatment at hospital.

item.title: 20 fishermen jailed for defying ilish netting ban in Chandpur
item.description:
A mobile court has sentenced 20 fishermen to different terms of imprisonment for catching ilish in the Padma-Meghna sanctuary in Chandpur, defying a fishing ban.
Of them, 13 fishermen were given 10 days in prison each, while the remaining seven received 15 days' imprisonment each. Each fisherman was also fined Tk 1,000, bringing the total fine to Tk 20,000.
The fishermen are residents of different villages in Laxmipur Model union under Chandpur Sadar upazila.
Md Mizanur Rahman, assistant fisheries officer of Sadar upazila, told UNB that a district task force, led by Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate Md. Najmul Huda, conducted the drive from 4:00pm to 9:00pm on Thursday.
During the drive, the team detained 20 fishermen and seized 30 kg of ilish, 35,000 metres of illegal monofilament fishing nets (locally known as current nets), and three engine-run fishing boats.
The seized ilish were distributed among an orphanage and needy people on Friday morning, while the boats were handed over to the Bangladesh Coast Guard for safekeeping.
The seized fishing nets were burnt in the presence of the executive magistrate.
A 22-day fishing ban in a 70-kilometre sanctuary along the Padma-Meghna rivers in Chandpur began on October 8 and will remain in force until midnight on October 29.
During the ban, catching, buying, selling, storing and transporting all types of fish, including ilish, in the designated rivers are prohibited.
District administration officials said violators will face imprisonment and fines under the law.

Dhaka's air quality remains 'unhealthy'
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality remained unhealthy on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 153 at 9:10am.
With this score, the capital ranked 12th among the world's most polluted cities.
Pakistan's Lahore, India's Delhi and Senegal's Dakar occupied the top three spots on the list, with AQI scores of 344, 244 and 184 respectively.
Earlier, at 9:20 am on Thursday, the city ranked 7th among the world's most polluted cities, recording an AQI score of 165.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups," and a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy," and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous," posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

Sri Lanka stun England with huge chase after Brook's double century
item.description:
Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook's record-setting knock.
The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.
South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.
Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.
Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.
Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.
Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.
Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka's blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook's earlier masterclass.
Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis was delighted at victory.
"I'm very happy as a captain," said Mendis. "Everyone believed we can do it. Every day we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score."
Brook was full of praise for Sri Lanka.
"Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400," said Brook, downplaying his double hundred.
"It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes."
Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.
He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs, by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.
Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.
Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.
Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50 and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.
The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.
Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.
